en.headline: Man from Hangzhou jailed seven months for importing 61200 duty-free cigarettes
en.dek: Customs said the 56-year-old was intercepted at the airport on 28 October with cigarettes valued at about HK$366000 and was also fined HK$1000.
body: A 56-year-old man who arrived from Hangzhou was sentenced to seven months’ imprisonment and fined HK$1000 on Monday after being convicted of importing duty-unpaid cigarettes and failing to declare them.

Customs officers intercepted him at Hong Kong International Airport on 28 October and found about 61200 duty-unpaid cigarettes in his luggage, with an estimated market value of HK$366000 and a duty value of about HK$202300.

Customs welcomed the sentence and said it reflected the seriousness of the offence. Under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance, handling, possessing or dealing in duty-unpaid cigarettes can carry a maximum fine of HK$2 million and seven years’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 杭州抵港旅客攜6.1萬支私煙 判囚7個月罰款千元
zh.dek: 海關指56歲男旅客於10月28日在機場被截獲，行李內有約61200支未完稅香煙，市值約36.6萬元。
body: 一名56歲從杭州抵港的男旅客周一在西九龍裁判法院被判監禁7個月及罰款1000元，罪名是進口未完稅香煙及未有申報。
海關人員於10月28日在香港國際機場截查該名旅客，在其行李內檢獲約61200支未完稅香煙，估計市值約36.6萬元，應課稅值約20.23萬元。
海關歡迎判刑，指監禁具阻嚇作用。根據《應課稅品條例》，處理、管有或售賣未完稅香煙最高可罰款200萬元及監禁7年。
